profile.reading: This Meta data center building (building 2 of 5 mapped in this cluster) is part of Meta's Los Lunas campus in Valencia County, New Mexico, south of Albuquerque. Meta broke ground here in 2016 with an initial $250 million building; a third data center opened in 2020, and Data Center Dynamics reported the campus had grown to seven buildings by 2023, with a two-building, roughly $800 million expansion then under construction, expected to take about three years and intended to support both current products and future AI hardware generations. The Village of Los Lunas has approved industrial revenue bonds to assist the build-out through Meta's Greater Kudu LLC affiliate, part of a financing structure the village has used across multiple expansion phases. On power, Meta and Public Service Company of New Mexico (PNM) marked commercial operation of the Route 66 Solar Facility in July 2022, a 49.5-megawatt, 450-plus-acre solar installation in neighboring Cibola County built by NextEra Energy Resources with more than 150,000 bifacial solar modules, built specifically to help supply renewable power to the Los Lunas data center. Meta's own fact sheet reports more than $2.5 billion invested in the New Mexico campus overall, roughly 400 operational jobs once complete, 1,100 peak skilled-trade construction workers, more than $4.9 million in direct funding to local schools and nonprofits, LEED Gold certification for campus buildings, and a Meta-supported total of 885 megawatts of new renewable energy plus 100 megawatts of battery storage added in New Mexico as part of Meta's global net-zero and 100%-renewable-electricity commitments. Meta does not publish a specific street address, exact building count, or per-building square footage for individual Los Lunas structures; the address above is derived from reverse-geocoding this building's mapped coordinates, not from an operator-published source, and should be treated as approximate.

profile.regional_context: Valencia County sits in the Albuquerque metro area along the historic Route 66 corridor, for which the Meta-linked Cibola County solar facility is named. New Mexico's data center growth has drawn on the state's high solar-resource potential and PNM's renewable-energy procurement, and Los Lunas has used industrial revenue bond financing repeatedly to support Meta's expansions, per Data Center Dynamics reporting on the village's approvals.

reading.body:
Meta's Los Lunas campus in Valencia County is a multi-building complex south of Albuquerque that has grown to seven operational buildings as of 2023, with a two-building expansion then under construction. Meta does not publish the total IT capacity or megawattage of the Los Lunas campus, so the scale of compute hosted here cannot be directly determined from operator specifications. The campus broke ground in 2016 and has received over $2.5 billion in Meta investment, with industrial revenue bond financing from the Village of Los Lunas supporting multiple expansion phases.

Power supply to Los Lunas is backed by dedicated solar generation: the Route 66 Solar Facility, a 49.5-megawatt installation in neighboring Cibola County built by NextEra Energy Resources and marked commercial in July 2022, was constructed specifically to supply renewable power to this data center. Meta reports 885 megawatts of new renewable energy and 100 megawatts of battery storage added across New Mexico as part of its global net-zero commitments; the Route 66 facility alone represents roughly 5.6 percent of that renewable total. Buildings on the Los Lunas campus hold LEED Gold certification. PNM supplies the grid connection, and New Mexico's high solar resource and renewable procurement policies have shaped the state's data center economics.

Los Lunas is one of 14 mapped data center facilities in New Mexico, but it is the only one with any published megawatt figure in this registry's coverage. No other data center operator in the state publishes IT capacity or power draw, making Los Lunas the sole basis for measuring New Mexico's current published data center footprint. This reflects Meta's transparency advantage over regional peers rather than a definitive statement about total compute in the state.
